question: GQ-001
subject: are the gates load-bearing? asked systematically instead of by accident
why: Yesterday I found by accident that a self-test passed 5 of 6 cases with the script it tested DELETED. The same question applies to every gate in the chain, and nothing had ever asked it.

what_it_proves_and_what_it_does_not.proves: every gate in the chain is INVOKED and its exit code is honoured
what_it_proves_and_what_it_does_not.does_not_prove: that a gate checks anything meaningful
what_it_proves_and_what_it_does_not.how_i_know: added a gate that prints one line and checks nothing — it reported PASS, because removing any named file makes the chain fail whether or not the file did work
what_it_proves_and_what_it_does_not.so: gate-selftest.sh answers the second question by breaking artifacts; this answers the first, which nothing did

the_finding_worth_keeping.what: appending "|| true" to one chain entry made ALL SIX real gates report FAIL
the_finding_worth_keeping.why: it swallows the exit code of everything downstream
the_finding_worth_keeping.significance: two words in package.json silently disable every gate at once, and nothing else in this repo would notice

two_artefacts_of_my_own_design_i_caught.what: BASELINE FAILED on the first run
two_artefacts_of_my_own_design_i_caught.cause: a scratch copy has one synthetic commit touching every watched path, so all 10 refresh triggers fire
two_artefacts_of_my_own_design_i_caught.verdict: the evaluator working correctly on artificial history, not a defect
two_artefacts_of_my_own_design_i_caught.fix: exclude the git-history gate from this chain; it has its own probe

two_artefacts_of_my_own_design_i_caught.cause: I excluded it from the chain and still tested removing it — the chain passed because it never invoked it
two_artefacts_of_my_own_design_i_caught.verdict: that reads as "not load-bearing" when the truth is "not tested"
two_artefacts_of_my_own_design_i_caught.fix: skip what the chain excludes, and say so
